You are an EFFICIENCY reviewer for a code-quality pass (not a bug hunt). Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim

Get the diff under review by running: `cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim && git diff HEAD~1..HEAD -- driver tests/andes_sim`

This is the F7 feature: `andes-sim run --model fast` transparent passthrough (resolve the built-in qemu engine, exec it with the user's post-`--` args). New: driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/run_passthrough.{cpp,hpp}. Modified: driver/engine_registry.cpp.

Your angle — EFFICIENCY: Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation, repeated I/O, blocking work added to a startup/hot path. Name the cheaper alternative.

The most important thing to investigate (READ engine_registry.cpp carefully — discover_engines() and builtin_qemu()):
- run_fast() in cmd_run.cpp calls `discover_engines()` and then picks out the "qemu" engine. Read what `discover_engines()` actually does: does it scan a directory and spawn `<bin> --describe` SUBPROCESSES (with a multi-second timeout each) for every Verilator engine binary it finds? If so, `--model fast` — which only needs the built-in qemu descriptor — pays the full discovery cost (multiple subprocess spawns + 5s-timeout exposure) at every invocation, including interactive/gdbstub runs where startup latency matters. 
- Is `builtin_qemu()` file-local (anonymous namespace)? Could the framework expose a cheap "just the built-in qemu descriptor" accessor (no directory scan, no subprocess) so fast mode skips discovering Verilator engines entirely? Quantify the wasted work (N subprocess spawns avoided).

Confirm by reading engine_registry.cpp and engine_registry.hpp. Only report HIGH-CONFIDENCE efficiency findings. For each: `file:line`, one-line `summary`, the concrete wasted work, and the cheaper alternative (name the function/accessor needed). Note any finding whose fix requires exposing a currently-file-local symbol. Do not hunt for correctness bugs. Return a concise findings list (or "no findings").

1	// Subprocess helpers for andes-sim.
2	//
3	// run_process spawns a child, captures its stdout, and kills it after a
4	// timeout -- the primitive the engine registry uses to ask `<bin> --describe`
5	// and the plan executor (F6) uses to run orchestrated legs. F5 extends this
6	// file with exec_passthrough (inherit stdio, no timeout) for fast/accurate.
7	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_PROCESS_HPP
8	#define ANDES_SIM_PROCESS_HPP
9	
10	#include <string>
11	#include <vector>
12	
13	namespace andes_sim {
14	
15	struct RunResult {
16	  int rc = -1;                // child exit status, or -1 if killed/abnormal
17	  std::string out;            // captured stdout
18	  bool timed_out = false;     // killed because it exceeded the timeout
19	  bool spawn_failed = false;  // pipe/fork failed before the child ran
20	};
21	
22	// Run argv (argv[0] resolved via PATH), capturing stdout. The child's stdin
23	// and stderr are redirected to /dev/null. If the child runs longer than
24	// timeout_ms it is SIGKILLed and timed_out is set.
25	RunResult run_process(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, int timeout_ms);
26	
27	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING this process's stdout and
28	// stderr (its output streams straight to the terminal) and stdin from
29	// /dev/null; chdir to `cwd` first if non-empty. No capture, no timeout. Returns
30	// the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was signalled, or -1 on spawn
31	// failure. Used by `build` to delegate to setup.sh / build_*.sh / make.
32	int run_inherit(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, const std::string& cwd);
33	
34	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING all three std streams
35	// (stdin, stdout, stderr) -- the transparent-passthrough mechanism behind
36	// `run --model fast|accurate`: the engine reads/writes the terminal directly,
37	// so an interactive gdbstub or semihosting console works unchanged. No chdir,
38	// no capture, no timeout. Returns the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was
39	// signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
40	int exec_passthrough(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
41	
42	}  // namespace andes_sim
43	
44	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_PROCESS_HPP

content.text: Let me get exact line numbers in cmd_run.cpp for the finding.

## Efficiency findings

**1. `driver/cmd_run.cpp:47` — `run_fast()` runs full engine discovery (N blocking subprocess spawns) to fetch only the built-in qemu descriptor.**

`run_fast()` calls `Discovery disc = discover_engines();` then immediately narrows to just `find_engine(disc, "qemu")`. But `discover_engines()` (engine_registry.cpp:148-165) builds the qemu descriptor *first and for free* (lines 152-154 via `builtin_qemu()`), then **unconditionally** scans `verilator/build` (or `$ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR`) and, for every `sim_*` binary it finds, spawns `<bin> --describe` as a blocking subprocess — engine_registry.cpp:80, `run_process({bin, "--describe"}, kDescribeTimeoutMs /*=5000*/)`, driven serially by `scan_dir` (lines 124-144). Every one of those discovered Verilator descriptors is then discarded by `run_fast`.

Concrete wasted work (this machine, right now): **N=5 subprocess spawns** — `sim_ax45mpv_mp2`, `sim_ax66_makatau`, `sim_d23`, `sim_ax46mpv_advanced`, `sim_ax45mpv_premium` (18-49 MB binaries each) — fork+execvp+poll+waitpid, serial, on the startup path of **every** `--model fast` run. This includes interactive `run --model fast ELF -- -gdb tcp::N -S` gdbstub/monitor launches, where the user waits through 5 Verilator `--describe` spawns before the gdbstub port even opens. Worst case is far worse: a sim binary that hangs on `--describe` burns the full 5 s timeout, so a bad scan dir is up to **N × 5 s = 25 s** of pure latency before qemu starts.

This work is provably useless for fast mode: `run_fast` already rejects `--engine != "qemu"` (cmd_run.cpp:40-45), so it can never consume any discovered Verilator engine.

**Cheaper alternative:** call `builtin_qemu()` directly instead of `discover_engines()`. `builtin_qemu()` (engine_registry.cpp:26-61) already produces exactly the descriptor fast mode needs — zero directory I/O, zero subprocess spawns. Replacing the discovery call with it eliminates all N spawns and the entire scan.

**Fix requires exposing a currently file-local symbol:** yes. `builtin_qemu()` lives in the anonymous namespace (engine_registry.cpp:19-146) and is not declared in engine_registry.hpp. The fix needs a public accessor — e.g. add `EngineDescriptor builtin_qemu();` to engine_registry.hpp (move it out of the anonymous namespace), or add a thin `builtin_engine("qemu")` wrapper — so `run_fast` can grab the built-in descriptor without triggering Verilator-engine discovery.

No other high-confidence efficiency findings in the diff. `run_passthrough.cpp` (single `build_argv` + one `insert`) and the new `standalone` invoke template in `builtin_qemu()` (one `push_back`) add no wasted work.
